Marissa / Lauren — thanks for taking this on. ClinTech (prospect) has asked for explicit language around on-prem/VPC deployments. Please incorporate the following ask list into a redlined Private Deployment Addendum and a short exhibit for Order Form:

- License grant: explicit runtime license to operate the specified model binary(s) within customer-managed infrastructure, including clarification on "derivative works" (they want to ensure outputs used in training of their downstream models are allowed)
- Snapshot/escrow-like access: propose a read-only encrypted snapshot delivery, with signed hash and a secure transfer window; include timing (within 10 business days of request) and attestation requirements
- Operator access: define scoped, time-limited engineer access for onboarding and emergency support; require pre-approved IP addresses and audit logging for any session
- Retention & evidence: list artifacts we will provide for audits (runbooks, signed custody logs, trace of model version + kernel used)
- Territory & sublicensing: limited carve-out wording for resellers (ClinTech resells to clinics); ensure we protect our distribution rights while allowing clinical resell under defined conditions
- Liability cap carveouts for on-prem modifications and data processing; propose a balanced compromise so sales can accept

Attachments: I'll attach the working draft I want redlined (draft_privdeploy_addendum_redlines.docx). If legal needs product clarification on operator access flows or snapshot format, ping me and I can bring in the runtime team.

Target: please return draft back to me by Friday EOD (10/01) so I can send to ClinTech early next week.

Best,
Vivek

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClinTech — please draft addendum redlines (priority)

Vivek / Lauren — attached is our first pass with comments (privdeploy_redline_comments.pdf). High-level notes:

- License scope: we can grant a runtime license limited to the specific model identifier + version; however, the language around "derivative works" needs tightening. Suggest we allow use of outputs for internal analytics and clinical workflows, but prohibit customer redistribution of model binaries or training our model with customer outputs unless we agree a separate training license.

- Snapshot/escrow: propose two-tier approach:
  * Tier A — managed snapshot delivery (our engineers produce an encrypted snapshot and hash); usable for audits but requires an approved custodian and attestation.
  * Tier B — full handover for long-term custody under escrow terms (additional fee, separate SOW).

- Operator access: require documented Just-In-Time access windows (max 8 hours per month as default) with MFA and session recording. Emergency access allowed with escalated approval (legal + customer security sig-off).

- Liability / indemnity: request narrower carveouts — we propose a mutual indemnity for clinical claims and maintain the standard cap on damages with carveouts only for gross negligence.

Questions for product (quick):
1) Can runtime produce an encrypted TAR with SHA256 and a signed manifest?
2) Do we have an operator ACL template (IP allowlist + session recording) we can attach as an exhibit?

If you confirm, I'll finalize language and produce a redlined PDF to send to Amelia.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference
(attachment: privdeploy_redline_comments.pdf)

Hi Amelia — appreciate the checklist. Attached is our redlined Private Deployment Addendum and a short exhibit describing snapshot delivery and operator access. Key points we addressed:

- Runtime license: explicit for the identified model(s) and runtime; output usage permitted for internal clinical workflows; redistribution of model binaries restricted unless separate agreement is signed.
- Snapshot delivery: encrypted TAR + SHA256 manifest, delivered via SFTP or signed transfer; standard turnaround within 10 business days; Tier B escrow available as paid option.
- Operator access: JIT windows, MFA, IP allowlist, session logging; emergency escalation path defined.
- Sublicensing: limited reseller carve-out for clinics with obligations to flow-down data protection duties; we included approved reseller playbook language.
- Liability: preserved mutual indemnities with limited carveouts for gross negligence; proposed $X cap (see redline).

Please review the redline (RDW_ClinTech_PrivDeploy_Addendum_20260930_redlined.pdf) and let us know any items you need clarified. If acceptable, I can circulate to procurement and legal on your side and prepare a DocuSign envelope.
